## eHoney | Computational-intensive analysis of honey-derived
environmental DNA information to disclose the
effect of climate change on biodiversity

## Project information

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Funding programme | EGI-ACE |
| Period | 2021–2022 |
| Research group | Animal and Food Genomics, University of Bologna |
| Status | Completed |


## Research team and collaboration

These research activities were carried out within
the [Animal and Food Genomics Group](https://site.unibo.it/animal-and-food-genomics/en)
at the University of Bologna, led by
[Prof. Luca Fontanesi](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/luca.fontanesi/en).

My contributions are presented within this
collaborative research context.


## Project overview

eHoney explored the computational analysis
of environmental DNA recovered from honey
as a source of information on biodiversity
and environmental signatures.

The project addressed the processing and
interpretation of sequencing data to
characterize biological components
represented in honey-derived DNA.


## My research contribution

My research activities focused on the
bioinformatic analysis of honey-derived
environmental DNA to recover biological
and genomic information from a complex
environmental matrix.

The computational approaches involved
the processing and interpretation of
sequencing data, the characterization
of biological components represented
in honey DNA and the investigation of
honey bee population genomic information.

These activities contributed to exploring
the potential of honey environmental DNA
for biodiversity monitoring and population
genomic applications.

::: {.project-methods}

**Methods & approaches**

NGS data analysis ·
Sequence alignment ·
Lowest Common Ancestor analysis ·
Database implementation

:::
